title: They Don't Get It, The Art of Being Understood
author: Empathy Elevated
summary: The fundamental leadership barrier is not that teams don't understand messages but that teams don't feel understood themselves, triggering defensive behavior that stops listening and causes emotional checkout. When people feel misunderstood, they stop receiving communication, become defensive, and emotionally disengage from work and relationships. This creates a bidirectional problem where leaders blame teams for not getting it while teams are actually blocking out input because they feel unheard and unseen. The article reframes the solution by arguing that the path to being understood starts with genuinely understanding others first, creating psychological safety through listening before expecting to be heard. Leaders who master empathetic understanding recognize that feeling understood is a prerequisite for team engagement, trust, and the openness required for any meaningful communication to land.
points: The core leadership challenge is not that teams don't understand leaders' messages but that teams don't feel understood themselves by their leaders.
When people feel misunderstood, they stop listening, become defensive, and emotionally check out from work and relationships.
The path to being understood starts with genuinely understanding others first, creating psychological safety through listening before expecting to be heard.
Leaders who fail to make teams feel understood trigger defensive behaviors that block all meaningful communication and reduce team engagement.
Psychological safety created through empathetic understanding is the foundation for teams to open up, trust leadership, and receive communication effectively.
quotes: The challenge most leaders face isn't that their team doesn't understand what they're saying.
The challenge is that their team doesn't feel understood themselves.
When people feel misunderstood, they stop listening. They become defensive. They check out emotionally.
The path to being understood starts with genuinely understanding others first.
Teams that feel understood develop stronger bonds, better performance, and greater openness to leadership communication.” Archived from Empathy Elevated on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
